# Performance Probing & Quality Settings
> Summary: The ENABLE_PROBING frame prober, editor quality presets, and the render settings they drive
> Scope: engine/runtime/source/util/prober.*, engine/editor/source/quality_preset.*, render/global.h

## Frame prober (`ENABLE_PROBING`)

- Implemented in `engine/runtime/source/util/prober.{h,cpp}`; **compiled out entirely** unless
  `ENABLE_PROBING` is defined.
- **Opt-in at generation time**: `./generate.sh --probing` (macOS) / `python dev/z1.py generate --probing`
  (all platforms) defines `ENABLE_PROBING` for the `Hybrid` configuration only. Plain `generate` (the
  default) produces probe-free projects in every configuration. The flag is baked into the generated
  Makefiles/`.vcxproj`, so **regenerate after toggling it**; `generate` prints the probing state it used
  and reports it in the `RESULT:` JSON (`"probing": true|false`).
- Flipping the flag is automated: `generate` detects the change, deletes `engine/intermediate/Hybrid` and
  warns that the next Hybrid build recompiles everything (objects do not depend on the generated projects,
  so without this the stale probe-enabled objects would silently survive).
- Distinct from `ENABLE_PROFILE` (CPU chrome-tracing of hot paths via `PROFILE_*` macros): probing is
  budget-oriented and reports both **CPU scopes and GPU frame time**.

| Macro | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `PROBE_CONFIGURE()` | reads the env knobs, applies the vsync override, creates the GPU query ring |
| `PROBE_FRAME_BEGIN()/END()` | frame wall-time sample, periodic `[probe]` reports, final summary |
| `PROBE_SCOPE("name")` | scoped wall-time sample (creates a variable; wrap in `{ }` if needed) |
| `PROBE_VALUE("name", v)` | raw counter sample (e.g. `draws`) |
| `PROBE_GPU_BEGIN_FRAME()/END_FRAME()` | `GL_TIME_ELAPSED` ring, driven from `OpenGLContext` |
| `PROBE_PRINT_SUMMARY()` | session summary (avg/min/max per scope) |

Env knobs (probing builds only): `Z1_PROBE_EVERY=N`, `Z1_PROBE_QUIET=1`, `Z1_PROBE_VSYNC=0|1`,
`Z1_PROBE_FINISH=1`, `Z1_PROBE_NO_GPU=1`, plus `Z1_NO_GL_CHECK=1` (error-polling cost A/B).

**macOS caveat:** `GL_QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE` usually stays false on the Apple GL driver unless the command
stream syncs, so GPU timer samples arrive only sporadically; `Z1_PROBE_FINISH=1` forces samples via a timed
`glFinish` but serialises the pipeline. Use pass-toggle deltas to attribute GPU cost. See
`docs/PROFILING_MACOS_OPENGL.md`.

## Camera-motion harness (probing builds, 2026-09-18)

Editor-side env knobs (`editor_layer.cpp`, compiled only with `ENABLE_PROBING`) to reproduce camera-motion
load without user input (scene scripts are blocked while the viewport is unfocused, so a real RMB drag
cannot be scripted):

- `Z1_AUTOROTATE=<deg/frame>` — rotate the primary camera every frame (0 = off)
- `Z1_AUTOROTATE_AXIS=x|y|z` — rotation axis (default y); `Z1_AUTOROTATE_STOP=<frame>` — stop at a frame
- `Z1_CAMROT_DISABLE=ao,bloom,taa,shadow,picking` — force-disable passes for attribution

Repro/verification: `Z1_AUTOROTATE=2 Z1_PROBE_EVERY=1 ./engine/bin/Hybrid/game --frames=600` and read the
per-frame `[probe]` reports (`Z1_PROBE_EVERY=1` gives one window per frame).

### Apple Intel driver shader recompile storms (root-caused 2026-09-18)

- **Symptom:** rotating the viewport camera dropped fps drastically (LOW 73→26, HIGH 91→45). Probe showed
  `renderer_draw` CPU at 0.7ms idle vs 25–40ms while rotating, **GPU flat (~5–6ms)** — CPU-bound, not GPU.
- **Mechanism:** `sample <pid>` showed ~94% of main-thread time inside the driver's shader compiler
  (`USC::CompilePixelShaderOpenGL`/IGC/vISA) invoked at draw time under the fullscreen passes (deferred
  lighting, AO). The compiles came in ~1s storms (90–220ms/frame) that started exactly when the visible
  draw set changed (an object entering/leaving the frustum) and decayed on their own.
- **Trigger:** image/UBO bindings were allocated from a LIFO stack, so the texture-unit layout depended on
  release history and **permuted every frame** (verified with a temporary GL state dump). The Apple Intel GL
  driver treats each sampler-unit layout as a new pipeline specialization; every new layout forced more
  JIT compiles, and each draw-set change introduced a batch of new layouts (hence the storms).
- **Fix:** allocate bindings lowest-free-first (`std::priority_queue` min-heaps in `graphics_context.h`).
  Layouts are now stable per frame and independent of visible content; verified: rotating run `renderer_draw`
  stays <1ms/frame with only the startup compile spike (HIGH: 45→~93fps avg incl. startup, GPU ~8.8ms).
- **Lesson for future perf work:** layout/history-dependent GL state that changes per frame is dangerous on
  macOS; keep per-frame state (bindings, unit assignments) deterministic. See also `render-pipeline.md`
  "Binding allocation stability".

## Quality presets (editor only)

- `engine/editor/source/quality_preset.{h,cpp}`: `QualityPreset` (`Low`/`Medium`/`High`) +
  `apply_quality_preset(GlobalSettings&, QualityPreset)`.
- Deliberately **not reflected** — game builds set the same settings from script; only the editor offers
  presets. The selector lives at the top of the global settings panel (`EditorLayer::show_quality_preset_selector`).
- Persisted as `quality_preset: <int>` in `editor_settings.yaml` (default `High` = previous engine defaults)
  and applied once at editor startup, after the initial scene load.

| Setting | LOW | MEDIUM | HIGH |
|---|---|---|---|
| `taa_enabled` / `taa_sharpen_enabled` | off / off | on / off | on / on |
| `ao_enabled` / `ao_resolution` / `ao_blur_enabled` | on / quarter / on | on / half / on | on / half / on |
| `pp_bloom_enabled` | off | on | on |
| `ssr_enabled` | off | untouched | untouched |
| `sm_resolution` / `sm_cascade_count` | 1024 / 1 | 2048 / 2 | 2048 / 4 |

Artistic values (AO radius/intensity, exposure, sun parameters) are never modified by a preset.

## Render-settings plumbing

- `GlobalSettings` (`render/global.h`) owns the features: `taa_enabled`, `pp_bloom_enabled`, `ssr_enabled`,
  `ao_enabled/ao_type/ao_resolution`, `sm_resolution`, `sm_cascade_count` (all reflected + serialized +
  Python-bound through `gen-pybinds`).
- `csm_cascade_count` is mirrored into the `Global` UBO as an `int` appended after `sky_sh`; the C++ mirror
  `GlobalConstants` is `alignas(16)` so the size assert is 784 (not 772). Keep
  `render/global.cpp::flush()`, `global.h` and `include/uniforms.glsl` in lockstep.
- **Renderers skip real work, not just uniforms**: with `taa_enabled == false` the velocity/TAA/sharpen
  passes are not added and the post-process pass consumes the scene color (or SSR output) directly; with
  `pp_bloom_enabled == false` the whole bloom chain is skipped. `add_bloom_pass(rg, input)` /
  `add_postprocess_pass(rg, target, scene_input, bloom_present)` take the chain inputs as parameters.
- `RenderShared::ensure_shadow_resources()` (called from `ensure_buffers()`) recreates the shadow depth
  array only when `sm_resolution`/`sm_cascade_count` changed; `calculate_csm_splits` computes N cascades
  (1–4) and `MAX_CSM_CASCADES` (4) is the array capacity. Shaders (`include/lighting.glsl`, `particle.glsl`)
  guard cascade selection with `u_csm_cascade_count` so missing layers are never sampled.
- AO buffers are allocated at `width / ao_resolution` (2 = half, 4 = quarter); a change recreates them
  through the existing size check in `ensure_buffers()`.

## macOS robustness

- The window advertises vsync but nothing applied it historically: `OpenGLContext::init()` now calls
  `glfwSwapInterval(is_v_sync_enabled() ? 1 : 0)`.
- `Window::is_display_available()` (monitor count > 0) gates layer/ImGui updates in `Application::run()` so a
  sleeping display no longer trips ImGui's multi-viewport monitor assert; rendering resumes on wake.
